dissonance

/DIS-uh-nunss/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Dissonance means a lack of harmony or agreement; a clashing quality in sounds, ideas, or values.

The music students winced at the dissonance when both pianos struck clashing chords at the same moment.

Example

Tomas prided himself on honesty, yet at his new sales job he found himself repeating small exaggerations from the official script. The dissonance between his personal values and his daily work left him uneasy every evening. Eventually he asked to rewrite the script so that he could believe every word he said.

This shows dissonance beyond music: the clash between what Tomas believes and what he actually does creates an uncomfortable inner conflict, which is exactly the kind of disagreement the noun names.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

discord: Discord is open disagreement or strife, usually between people - a family or committee in discord is quarreling. Dissonance is the clashing quality itself, and it needs no quarrel: two chords, or your own values and actions, can produce dissonance with nobody arguing at all.

clash: A clash is the collision moment itself - two colors, two egos, two schedules meeting head-on - and the word is blunt and everyday. Dissonance is the more formal, sustained lack of harmony that hangs in the air afterward: not the bang of the collision but the ongoing off-key quality it leaves.

friction: Friction is the heat of people rubbing against each other - irritation and tension building between coworkers or allies. Dissonance is cooler and more abstract: a lack of fit between sounds, ideas, or values. Friction needs people in contact; dissonance can sit inside one mind, between belief and behavior.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

harmony: a pleasing, balanced agreement

accord: a state of agreement

Where it sits · how severe the clash of parts is — mismatch → dissonance → cacophony

mismatch vs. dissonance: A mismatch is a mild difference between things, while dissonance is a genuine clash that feels uncomfortable to hear or think about.

cacophony vs. dissonance: Cacophony is stronger than dissonance; dissonance is a clash between elements, while cacophony is a whole wall of harsh, jumbled noise.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart, not

Root — son

Root — son: from Latin sonare, to sound

Suffix — -ance

Suffix — -ance: noun-forming ending; a state or quality

Put it together

Put it together: Dissonance combines dis-, meaning apart, with the Latin sonare, to sound, plus the noun ending -ance: literally a state of sounding apart. The son- root is highly productive in English, appearing in sonic, resonance, and unison.

Use the root in a new word: unison

Use the root in a new word: unison: The choir held the final note in perfect unison, every voice sounding as one.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal; academic and musical

Dissonance is always a noun: you hear dissonance in clashing chords, feel cognitive dissonance when your actions contradict your beliefs, and notice dissonance between two policies. The adjective form, discordant, describes something that itself lacks harmony; keep dissonance for naming the clash itself.
